thread:
Jordan: Heads up — seeing cases where the placement proxy admits a prewarm lease but the central orchestrator's ledger never shows the lease. Results in double-warm and billing mismatches. Anyone else hit this?
Liam: Yea, saw a spike yesterday. Proxy log shows admit at t=12:03:15. Central ledger entry only appears ~2s later, sometimes not at all.
Sofia: My hunch: proxy does optimistic admit for latency, central persists async. If central write fails (transient DB partition) proxy keeps serving.
Maria: That's a dangerous split. We need firm ownership semantics: who is the source of truth for 'active' leases and who can evict?
Jordan: Proposal sketch: proxy owns transient admission for fast-path, central owns durable lease + billing. But proxy must reconcile and back off if central never persisted.
Liam: ok but what about failover — if controller restarts and central ledger is stale, proxies might be admitting conflicting leases.
Sofia: Could add an acknowledgement hop: proxy sends admit -> central synchronously but blocks only up to X ms. If ack received, treat as durable. If not, proxy falls back to conservative admission (no double-warm).
Maria: Tradeoffs: adds ~1-3ms tail on warm-path, but avoids cost of duplicate prewarm. We can make X configurable per tenant/SLO.
Jordan: Agreed. Also need a correlation id so we can join proxy admit events and central writes in traces/metrics. I propose request_id per admit, propagated everywhere.
Sofia: Example header we can use: X-Ext-Req: <uuid>. Proxy logs: admit id + req; central ledger log includes same id. Then we can run queries to prove consistency.
Jordan: ```
# example lease request payload
POST /v1/leases
{
  "tenant": "acme",
  "lease_type": "prewarm",
  "req_id": "8a1f-...-c3d2"
}
```
Liam: Observability gap today: proxy metrics are sampled at 10s resolution, central at 60s. Need finer sampling + traces. Without that we can't root-cause intermittent misses.
Maria: Ops action: add a high-cardinality tag for req_id in our trace logs, and add a debug sampler for placement proxy for 1% of requests.
Sofia: Policy question: if proxy doesn't get ack and still admits (after timeout), should it attach a 'tentative' flag that forces central billing to do reconciliation later?
Jordan: I prefer tentative + eventual reconcile. That way admission is fast but there's an explicit reconciliation path to fix billing/eviction.
Liam: For reconciliation: run job that matches proxy admits without central counterpart older than N secs and either retro-charge or evict prewarm. Need UX decision.
Maria: Also add an alert for reconciliation backlog > threshold. We had a day where backlog hit 3000 and cost spiked.
deploy-bot: @channel canary deploy of placement-proxy v2 (req-id + ack path) scheduled Tue 03:00 UTC. :rocket:
infra-bot: Note: will need a short DB migration to add req_id index to ledger table; migration window 5m.
Jordan: Next steps we agreed on: implement req_id propagation, synchronous ack with configurable timeout X, tentative admit flag, reconciliation job, and telemetry sampler. @Sofia to own POC, @Liam to run perf numbers on added tail, @Maria to add alerting. :thumbsup:
Sofia: I'll open the PR and a short design doc with perf numbers and toggles for X.
Liam: I'll simulate failure modes and measure 50/95/99 latencies.
Maria: I'll add reconciliation playbook and cost alarms.
Jordan: Thanks — let's regroup after POC tests.
